en: The Essential Dharma of the Deva Maheśvara:
At that time, the Deva Maheśvara was sporting with various celestial maidens in the Heaven of Delighting in Transformations (Nirmāṇarati), performing various musical performances.
Suddenly, a celestial maiden manifested from within his hair; her countenance—
He was of perfect countenance and foremost in artistic skill;
among the hosts of devas, none could surpass him.
He then spoke this mantra:
*Namo urasamabhyo śikhādivyaprabhṛtaye śīghrakarāya saṃkule saṃkule dantye tadyathā svabhānodike ca varāmanorine hūṃ phaṭ.* Whoever maintains the recitation of this mantra:
One does not inquire whether they are pure or impure,
whether they have a wife or are without one,
or whether they consume the five pungent roots, alcohol, and meat, or abstain from them.
Those who constantly recite and uphold [this] shall have all their virtuous aspirations fully accomplished;
how much more so for those whose three karmas are pure, who will swiftly attain *siddhi*.
What further doubt could there be?
If there is anyone who, at the time of sunset,
recites this mantra one hundred and eight times, [they shall attain liberation].
It will immediately produce efficacious results.
Next is the method for painting the image: first, paint an image of the deity Maheśvara, with a countenance that is extraordinary, upright, and exquisitely beautiful.
From the hairline, a celestial maiden was manifested,
her beauty unsurpassed, draped with exquisite necklaces and adorned with bracelets and armlets upon both wrists.
The left hand cradles a celestial flower,
while the face displays a joyful and charming expression as it gazes toward the Heavenly King;
the right hand is positioned downward in the gesture of grasping the hem of the skirt.
The goddess Mātaṅgī sits upon the left knee.
Next, the characteristics of the hand mudrā are explained:
the two hands are crossed externally.

Pressing the left hand down and forming the binding with the right, extend the *dāna* (thumb), *vīrya* (forefinger), and *bala* (middle finger) fingers while joining the *dhyāna* (ring finger) and *prajñā* (little finger); with the *dhyāna* and *yau* [fingers] joined, this constitutes the mudrā for invocation.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vītarāse parāmṛtāṇi cindani cindani bindani bindani svāhā. If there be anyone who daily receives and maintains this seal-mantra (mudrā-mantra), [they shall attain success].
Those who make offerings to the deity Maheśvara obtain various efficacious results;
they also frequently perform this mudrā and mantra.
It makes offerings to all Buddhas,
causing all Buddhas to rejoice;
furthermore, it effectively cures all manner of illnesses.
If one recites this one thousand times,
it will cause the wife to feel great joy;
if one recites it two thousand times, [the same result follows].
It causes all people to give rise to joy;
if one recites it three thousand times,
one will be loved and cherished by non-humans.
If recited four thousand times,
all the vināyaka spirits will rejoice.
If recited five thousand times, [the same result follows].
All the nāga maidens will give rise to a heart of joy;
even by reciting it ten thousand times,
all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and ṛṣis possessing the five supernatural powers will be entirely delighted.
If a person wishes to see their own original body,
they should take the remaining firewood from a cremated corpse,
recite the mantra one hundred and eight times, and summon it.
One will immediately behold one's own original body.
Furthermore, if there is a method for subduing an enemy,
take red earth and draw their form.
Write down their names and step upon them with your left foot,
reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Regardless of distance, that person will naturally come to submit to one’s command.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause a husband and wife to love each other,
one should paint their images and write down their names.
Tread upon it according to the previous ritual;
then they will immediately come to love and respect one another.
Furthermore, if one wishes to obtain the love and respect of kings, ministers, and all people, [one should perform this rite].
Perform it according to the preceding ritual.
If one is treating a disease caused by spirits,
take *gāḍha* wood.
Cut it into twenty-one pieces.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times;
burn one piece with each recitation, and the illness will be cured.
If it is a disease caused by spirits,
take asafoetida, agallochum, realgar, blue pine (śrīveṣṭaka), and leaves of *kṛtavedhana*;
taking equal parts of each, grind and sift them, then mix with water to form pills.
If one recites the mantra while burning these, the illness will be cured immediately.
If it is a case of *kṣudrakarma* (sorcery or bewitchment),
take realgar, agallochum, *kaṅkola*, *śuṇṭhī*, *vatsanābha*, the urine of a ram, the hoof-horn of a white horse, and the dung of a donkey.
Divide each of these eight substances into portions and burn them;
fumigate with the smoke through the nostrils and smear it upon the body.
If one wishes to perform the rite of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*), [one should do so].
Recite the mantra over water seven times and sprinkle it in the four directions;
according to one's preference for distance, the boundary shall be established in accordance with the Dharma.
The Essential Dharma of the Heavenly King Maheśvara: Within this dharma, Maheśvara refers to Īśāna, the deity of the northeast.
